title: Free Income Statement Template: P&L Worksheet and Excel
desc: Prepare a simple period income statement with net sales, COGS, operating costs and profit checks. Use the browser worksheet or download the original Excel template.
example: The fictional workshop earned $12,000 gross sales, with $0 returns, $5,500 reviewed COGS, $3,000 other operating expenses and $200 depreciation. Other income, interest and entered tax are zero. Net sales are $12,000, gross profit $6,500, operating profit $3,300 and net income $3,300. A negative result is shown as a loss, not rejected or hidden.
scope: This is a simplified historical period P&L, not a cash report, transaction ledger, tax calculator or a complete financial-statement pack. Enter earned revenue and the expenses belonging to the same period under your reviewed basis. The tool does not determine recognition or calculate COGS, depreciation or tax. In this sole-owner teaching model, equipment purchases, loan principal and owner draws are not entered as operating expenses. The limited rows do not cover every business or entity.
formula: Net sales = gross sales − returns. Gross profit = net sales − entered COGS. Operating profit = gross profit − other operating expenses − depreciation. Net income = operating profit + other income − interest − entered income-tax expense. Every money input is a nonnegative USD amount; signed calculated profit/loss is allowed. Returns greater than sales require a different presentation and are rejected in this simplified model.

title: Free Cash Flow Statement Template: Historical Worksheet and Excel
desc: Classify historical operating, investing and financing cash movements, reconcile closing cash and download an original Excel template with a filled example.
example: The fictional sample starts with $10,000 cash. Operating cash is $11,000 − $4,500 − $3,000 = $3,500. Investing cash is −$1,000. Financing cash is $2,000 − $500 − $600 = $900. Net change is $3,400 and calculated closing cash is $13,400. The independently entered closing figure is $13,400, so the difference is $0. Change that independent figure to $13,300 to reveal a $100 mismatch; do not overwrite source records simply to force a tie.
scope: This simplified direct-method historical worksheet is not a forecast, a forecast-versus-actual variance report or a certified statutory statement. It covers the listed categories only, in USD. It excludes taxes, interest, foreign exchange, noncash transactions and other categories; do not silently place unsupported transactions into a convenient row. Confirm the account scope and framework-specific classification with your accountant. The sole-owner withdrawal presentation is a stated teaching assumption, not a rule for corporate payroll or dividends.
formula: Operating = customer receipts − supplier payments − other operating payments. Investing = equipment disposal receipts − equipment purchases. Financing = borrowing + owner contributions − principal repayment − sole-owner withdrawals. Calculated closing = opening + operating + investing + financing. Difference = calculated closing − independently reconciled closing. Zero means only that the entered figures tie. Internal transfers between included accounts are excluded from consolidated movements.

title: Free Startup Budget Template: Costs, Reserve and Funding Gap
desc: Separate startup spending from retained cash, model a fixed early-trading horizon and calculate a funding gap. Includes an original Excel template and browser worksheet.
fields: Fixed entered monthly operating cash payments
Fixed entered monthly customer cash receipts
Cash to retain at horizon end
report: Modeled end cash after listed uses
example: The fictional startup lists $10,000 equipment, $2,000 setup, $1,000 deposits and $1,000 contingency: $14,000 upfront cash uses. Monthly payments of $3,000 less receipts of $1,000 leave a $2,000 monthly cash need. Three months require $6,000. Add a $4,000 retained closing reserve to reach a $24,000 funding target. Available funding of $23,000 leaves a $1,000 gap and $3,000 modeled end cash. The $4,000 reserve is retained cash, not an extra expense or supplier payment.
scope: This is a bounded startup funding worksheet, not a full business plan, valuation, profit forecast or dated runway model. Monthly receipts and payments stay constant for 1–24 entered trading months. It assumes upfront funding arrives before spending and does not model within-month payment order, ramp-up, seasonality, financing fees or loan repayment unless already included in the supported cash assumptions. Model pre-opening delays separately. Positive monthly cash generation is not used to reduce the upfront funding target in this deliberately conservative model.
formula: Upfront uses = equipment + setup + refundable deposits + entered contingency. Operating shortfall = max(0, monthly payments − monthly receipts) × months. Funding target = upfront uses + operating shortfall + retained reserve. Surplus/(gap) = entered funding − target. End cash = funding − upfront uses + (monthly receipts − monthly payments) × months. End cash can be negative; it does not test daily solvency. Deposits and equipment are cash uses here, not automatically profit expenses. Replace each assumption with source evidence and use the dated forecast for timing.
